summary: Elizabeth Stuart is a religious studies scholar who founded Theology & Sexuality and served as a director at the University of Winchester in 2021.

Elke Rogersdotter specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. She earned her PhD at Umeå University (attested 2006) under supervisor Thomas B. Larsson, supervisor Bozena Werbart, and co-advisors Karin Viklund and P. Ajithprasad.
Ellen M. Raven is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology who held posts at Leiden University, attested in 2003 and on the Editorial Board in 2018.
Elliot M. Stern is an Indology scholar who completed his Ph.D. studies at the University of Pennsylvania by 1998.

Elliot Sperling (1951–2017) was a Tibetology and history scholar. He studied at Queens College and Indiana University under Helmut Hoffmann and Lynn Struve, later holding posts at Indiana University (1987–2015), Harvard (1992–1993), and the University of Delhi.

Ellison Banks Findly is a religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Fred Pfeil. She held posts at Mount Holyoke College and Trinity College, Hartford, serving as associate professor of religion and Asian studies (attested 1989).
Emanuela Garatti is a Tibetology scholar who has held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Munich (attested 2018).

Embar Krishnamacharya was an Indologist who served as a Pandit at the Oriental Manuscripts Library and Research Institute and held posts at Sanskrit Pathashala, Vadtal (attested 1937) and Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (attested 1939).

Emi Matsushita is an archaeologist and historian who studied at Nanzan University, the University of East Anglia, and Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. She held posts at Shizuoka Prefectural Board of Education and Ohio State University.
Emil Krebs (1867–1930) was a sinologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Breslau and Humboldt University of Berlin, where his teachers included Wilhelm Grube.

Emil Rödiger (1801–1874) was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg, later serving as professor of Oriental languages there (1830–1860) and at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1860.

Emil Schlagintweit (1835–1904) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Franz Joseph Lauth and became a corresponding member of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 1864.

Emil Sieg (1866–1951) was an Indologist and linguist. Educated at Berlin, Munich, Tübingen, and Göttingen under Weber, Kielhorn, and Kuhn, he held chairs and professorships at Berlin, Kiel University, and the University of Göttingen.

Emilio Teza (1831–1912) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Anton Boller. He held professorships at the Universities of Bologna, Pisa (~1860–1886), and Padua (~1886–1906), alongside librarian posts in Venice and Florence.

Emily T. Yeh is a Tibetology scholar who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and the University of California, Berkeley. She joined the faculty at the University of Colorado around 2003.
Emma Georgina Rothschild is a historian who studied at Somerville College, Oxford, and MIT. She held professorships at the University of Cambridge (~1988) and Harvard University (~2008).

Emmie te Nijenhuis is an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. She served as associate professor of Indian musicology at Utrecht University (1964–1988) and held a post at the University of Amsterdam (~1970–1996).

Enamul Haque (1937–2022) was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Dhaka and the University of Oxford. He served as Director General of the Bangladesh National Museum (1983–1991) and headed the International Centre for Bengal Art.

Encho Tamura (1917–2013) was a Buddhist studies and history scholar educated at Kyushu and Kyoto universities. He served as professor at Kumamoto University (~1968–1982) and Kyushu University (1968–1980), and directed the Kyushu Historical Museum.

Endo Asai (1927–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He served as professor at Rissho University (1972–1997) and president of Minobusan University (1998–2001).
